hook: The king of the Huns, called the Scourge of God.

pages.x: Attila was born around 406 into the ruling family of the Huns, horsemen from the steppes who had swept into Europe. In 434 he and his brother Bleda inherited the throne. Around 445 Bleda died, probably murdered by Attila, who ruled alone from the plains of Hungary.

His armies of mounted archers ravaged the Eastern Roman Empire, destroying dozens of cities in the Balkans, and forced the emperor to pay him 2,100 pounds of gold a year. Christians called him the Scourge of God, sent to punish them for their sins.

In 450 Honoria, the Western Roman emperor's sister, sent Attila her ring and begged him to save her from a marriage she did not want. Attila said this was a proposal, and demanded half of the Western Empire as his dowry. When he was refused, he invaded Gaul.
In 451, deep in Gaul, he was met by an army of Romans and Visigoths under the general Aetius on the Catalaunian Plains. It was one of the bloodiest battles of the age, and Attila pulled back.

In 452 he invaded Italy and destroyed the city of Aquileia; its refugees fled into the lagoons and helped found Venice. Pope Leo I rode out to meet him, and Attila turned back without attacking Rome. Legend says Saints Peter and Paul appeared beside the pope with swords.

pages.x: In 453 he married a young woman named Ildico. In the morning he was found dead, choked by a burst blood vessel. Legend says he was buried in three coffins, of gold, silver and iron, and that the men who buried him were killed to keep the place a secret.
Attila's empire fell apart soon after his death, but his raids helped weaken the Western Roman Empire, which fell 23 years later. His name became a byword for a ruthless conqueror.
pts: Ruled the Hunnic Empire at its height
Ravaged the Balkans, Gaul and Italy
Helped bring down the Western Roman Empire
